pr_title: Fall through malformed JWTs to subsequent realms in the chain
pr_body:
Invalid JWTs do not immediately fail the authentication process when
the first JWT realm in the chain fails to parse them.
Instead, subsequent realms in the chain get their chance
to try parse a token out of the `Bearer` scheme.

Introduces `Authenticator.Context#getApiKeyString` method to
be able to more easily track where the API Key credential is used.

Fixes https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/issues/101367
pr_comments: Hi @albertzaharovits, I've created a changelog YAML for you.

issue_context.title: Bearer token interpreted as malformed JWT blocks custom realms and anonymous access
issue_context.body:
[Anonymous access](https://www.elastic.co/guide/en/elasticsearch/reference/current/anonymous-access.html) and [custom authn realms](https://www.elastic.co/guide/en/elasticsearch/reference/current/custom-realms.html) don't work correctly when there's a JWT realm configured in the chain. 

The JWT realm is too eager to parse the `Authorization: Bearer <token>` request header.
If a JWT realm encounters a bearer token that it cannot parse, it fails the authentication altogether. This prevents other (custom) realms, that follow a JWT realm in the chain, to be consulted for parsing and validating the bearer token. This also prevents incoming requests to be considered as "anonymous" if no authentication token can be extracted from the incoming request.
comments: We've discussed this in yesterday's team meeting, and agreed that anonymous access SHOULD NOT be permitted if the `Bearer` scheme uses an invalid JWT token, but that custom realms, following any JWT realm in the chain, SHOULD be allowed to try parse the `Bearer` credential.

review_comments:
This presumes the bearer token is an encoded JWT. That's probably a safe bet, but not required. If it is not a JWT then attempts to parse as JWT will raise an exception which here is exceptionally expensive. Can we include an additional check above `if(userCredentials.toString().contains(".") == false) return null ) ? It's not perfect, but could help to short circuit non JWT tokens. (FWIW '.' is not a base64 character nor is it a valid character in a UUID so any non JWT likely won't include a '.')

Also, I think checking for a '.' will help ensure any token service tokens that failed in the oauth2 validator will fail faster here and consume fewer resources.

Good point about the fail fast when the token doesn't have dots.
I've pushed [255c533](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/pull/101660/commits/255c5333c5ef75fc2dd3a512d26505bcd9f9cbbd) that actually checks for 2 dots (the minimum for a valid JWT), also without using `.toString`.

nit: I think there might be a tiny difference w.r.t. the elder behavior. I haven't fully tested but I think the elder behavior would only allow anonymous access for `Bearer ` but not `Bearer  ` (note one vs. multiple spaces). I could be wrong and it probably doesn't matter and it was probably was never the intention to be white space dependent. I could also be totally wrong, but thought it worth a mention in case you think it matters. (I pulled `header.regionMatches(true, 0, "Bearer ", 0, "Bearer ".length()) && header.length() > "Bearer ".length()` into my IDE to get a better sense of exactly what that does and is the basis of this comment)

> nit: I think there might be a tiny difference w.r.t. the elder behavior. I haven't fully tested but I think the elder behavior would only allow anonymous access for Bearer but not Bearer

I think the behavior, whatever that is, stays unchanged from this PR.
The method to extract the bearer token hasn't changed in this PR (the redundant one from `AuthenticatorChain#shouldFallbackToAnonymous` was identical to the reused `Authenticator#extractBearerTokenFromHeader`).

After debugging, it looks like both `Bearer ` and `Bearer  ` get truncated to `Bearer` in the netty http decoder (somewhere, havent't pinpointed it precisely), which means that ES (both before and after this PR) interprets it as if there's no bearer credential present (so anonymous is allowed).
